Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear questions. Answers below (high-level) and I've attached our Retention Playbook + an SLA worksheet for erasures. Looping in Rishi (Security) and Irene (Data Governance) for any technical addenda.

1) Geographical storage:
- Primary: Customer requests land in the region of the nearest active Redwood region by default (US: us-west-2 for west coast customers; us-east-1 for east coast).
- Administrative logs and control-plane metadata are stored in the US unless a specific region-lock is requested as part of an Enterprise or Private deployment.

2) Retention window:
- Hosted (default): request payloads and generation artifacts are retained for up to 30 days for debugging and abuse detection; ephemeral KV/prefix caches expire on a policy window (commonly 1–7 days) depending on workload type.
- For Enterprise tier with retention controls enabled: retention can be shortened to as low as 0 days (no retention) or extended under contract; Dedicated/Private customers generally specify retention in the contract.

3) Account-level erasure (customer-initiated):
- Expected timeline: 7–30 days depending on scope and backups. Our standard flow: request intake -> identity verification -> scheduled purge across hot stores -> verification of purge from backups and caches -> confirmation to customer. The Playbook attachment maps this in detail.

Attachments: HostedAPI_Retention_Playbook_v2.pdf (retention maps, cache TTLs, purge workflow), data-deletion-sla.xlsx (timelines by storage tier).

Let me know if you want a compact one-page response for your SOC pack; we can drop a version that includes only the bullet answers and the SLA table.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen\Senior Solutions Engineer, Security & Compliance\Redwood Inference\attachments: HostedAPI_Retention_Playbook_v2.pdf, data-deletion-sla.xlsx

Stephanie / Irene — quick technical clarifications for the playbook (cc'd):
- Backups: automated snapshots are retained for 90 days in core Hosted; these snapshots are immutable for restoration and require a separate certified purge process; we should surface that to the customer (timeline extension).
- Cache TTLs: prefix/KV caches are typically 24–72 hours unless long-tail workloads request sticky caching; note that caches do not persist to long-term backups.
- Logs: audit logs that contain metadata about requests are stored for 365 days for security/audit reasons, but these logs do not include full request payload content (payloads follow the 30-day policy).

Recommend we explicitly call out: backups (90d) vs request payloads (30d) vs logs (365d). Also add the fallback behavior when region-lock is requested during onboarding (requests routed to the requested region; control plane still in US unless Private).

-Rishi
Lead, Platform Security

Adding a data-governance note for the customer-facing copy:
- Erasure scope: we classify erasure requests into three scopes: (1) request-level (individual prompt/completion), (2) account-level (all customer data for a tenant), (3) legal hold exemptions (requires legal review). For (1) we can usually complete within 24–72 hours; for (2) the standard cross-system purge and verification is 7–30 days; for (3) timeline depends on legal process.
- Evidence: after purge we provide a signed confirmation and a purge log that lists systems processed (hotstore, cache, control-plane records).

I'll tidy this into a short paragraph for the SOC pack; flagged one minor correction in the Playbook where we referenced a 60d snapshot retention — that should read 90d.

—Irene
Senior Data Governance Manager

Hi Samantha — following up with the concise language for your SOC pack (below) and attached the corrected Playbook and SLA spreadsheet.

Summary for SOC pack (please paste into your questionnaire):
- Residency: by default, request payloads are routed to and stored in the nearest Redwood region. Administrative/control-plane metadata is kept in the US; region-locking to a single geography is supported for Enterprise and Private customers.
- Retention (standard Hosted): request payloads and generation artifacts retained up to 30 days; prefix/KV caches 1–7 days (workload dependent); automated snapshots/backups retained 90 days (used for disaster recovery, require certified purge); audit logs retained 365 days (metadata-only).
- Erasure: account-level erasures: 7–30 days depending on backup scope. Request-level erasures: typically 24–72 hours. After completion, we provide a purge certificate and a log of systems processed. Exceptions for legal holds require review.

Attachments included: HostedAPI_Retention_Playbook_v2.pdf (corrected), data-deletion-sla.xlsx (timeline by storage tier).
